alejandra (DevEx): Heads up — hit a weird auth/rotation casing in the node SDK while onboarding a customer. Background workers still used the old key after rotation.

sam: Ugh. Which env vars are in play?

alejandra (DevEx): The sample app and our daemon use different conventions. In the app we set REDWOOD_API_KEY, but the daemon image expects REDWOOD_KEY. Also we have REDWOOD_ORG / REDWOOD_PROJECT for scoping.

mira: Can you paste the minimal repro? Logs + env dump (redacted) would help.

alejandra (DevEx): Repro is tiny — single container with SDK v1.4.2, rotate key in console, hit /health which triggers background sync. After rotation the sync still shows old key in outbound header: 
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-old-xxxxx
x-redwood-org: org-acme
```
The app web requests pick up sk-new-xxxxx immediately. Only the worker keeps old. :thinking_face: 

sam: Might be credential caching in the SDK. We cache a token provider for 10m by default. Did you set REDWOOD_CREDENTIAL_CACHE=0?

alejandra (DevEx): I tried forcing cache ttl=0 and restarted the worker — same result. The process doesn't even attempt a token refresh (no network call in logs).

tyler: SDK parity note — python SDK rotated credentials on cache miss correctly (we added a refresh hook), node didn't. Could be missing watch for env var changes or signal handling.

mira: Are we shipping an official env var precedence table in docs? I remember ambiguity between REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_KEY, and RW_API_TOKEN in some sample apps. That causes onboarding friction.

alejandra (DevEx): We don't. That's part of the problem. New customer used RW_API_TOKEN in their k8s secret, our quickstart used REDWOOD_API_KEY, internal daemon image used REDWOOD_KEY. Everyone assumes theirs is canonical.

ci-bot: build #4821 on main succeeded (<https://ci.redwood.ai/build/4821|view>).

sam: Proposal: (1) Add env var precedence table to SDK readmes + quickstart (2) Align daemon images to accept all three names for next minor, with warning logs if multiple set (3) Fix node SDK to watch for env rotations / provide an explicit rotate() API and a cache TTL env var.

mira: +1. Also log a distinct message when a key is loaded from env vs credential provider — makes support triage easier.

tyler: I'll file a PR to node-sdk for rotate()/watch and add tests for a simulated rotation. I'll also add an opt-in 'watchEnv=true' flag rather than auto-polling so we don't surprise customers with perf hit.

alejandra (DevEx): Thanks. For docs I'll draft an 'Auth in Tooling' quickstart that shows recommended vars: primary REDWOOD_API_KEY, fallbacks RW_API_TOKEN then REDWOOD_KEY; show scoped header usage: X-Redwood-Organization and X-Redwood-Project, and note rotation steps.

mira: Can we add an example k8s secret + deployment snippet showing how to do zero-downtime rotation (create new secret, patch deployment with envFrom to trigger restart)? That will cut a lot of support tickets.

alejandra (DevEx): Yup. I'll put that in the draft. Action items: Tyler -> node-sdk PR (rotate + watchEnv) by EOD Thu, Mira -> docs precedence table + k8s rotation snippet by Fri, Sam -> add warning logs to daemon images and accept aliases. I'll open tickets and link here.

tyler: Starting a ticket: <https://rwd/issues/DEVX-2219|DEVX-2219> node-sdk rotate/watch API.

alejandra (DevEx): Filed docs ticket: <https://rwd/issues/DEVX-2220|DEVX-2220> auth env var precedence + k8s rotation guide.

mira: Adding support triage checklist to runbook once PRs land. Thanks everyone :rocket:

sam: If anyone sees other SDKs doing weird fallback behavior, drop examples here and we'll standardize.

alejandra (DevEx): Copy — will paste a short sampleapp that demonstrates the problem so test coverage covers it.

(End)
